newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold, silver close lower on higher supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold, silver close lower on higher supply.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carats closes 40 rupees lower at 4,830 rupees per 10 grammes on improved supplies of imported metal following a downtrend in world prices.
** Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) close 400 rupees lower at 56,500 rupees per piece.
** Silver .999 closes 10 rupees lower at 6,930 rupees after opening 10 rupees higher at 6,950 rupees per kg.
Standard gold opened 20 rupees lower at 4,830 rupees per 10 grammes and fell further by another 20 rupees during the day to end at 4,810 rupees due to improved supplies, dealers said.
The reopening of bullion markets after a four-day holiday in the Gulf had resulted in an increased inflow of imported gold, the dealers said.
"Indian expatriates in the Gulf are bringing gold after a brief lull," said Bombay Bullion Association president M.L. Damani. "I expect the improved supplies to be met with matching demand."
"Marriage season demand is good. I expect prices to be steady in the near term," he said.
Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) closed 400 rupees lower at 56,300 per piece following improved supplies.
Silver, which opened 10 rupees higher at 6,950 rupees per kg, however, ended losing 10 rupees to 6,930 rupees per kg under selling pressure.
Dealers said speculative selling and mild profit-taking had led to the fall in silver prices. (Conversion $1=35.77 rupees)
